title: Transformer-Based Network Intrusion Detection System
subtitle: Intelligent Multi-Class Cyber Attack Classification
notes: Transformer-Based Network Intrusion Detection System for Intelligent Multi-Class Cyber Attack Classification; add student and institutional details.

title: Scope of the completed implementation
body: Seven-class flow classifier and controlled baselines
Chronological attention and endpoint graph context
TabTransformer, flow-grid ViT and BERT-style encoder
SHAP/LIME, FedAvg and supervised online learning
Passive PCAP pipeline; live interface path provided

title: Network inputs
body: 24 flow statistics: duration, sizes, rates, intervals and flags
Context: source/destination ports and protocol
IP private-status indicators and stable hash buckets
Raw IPs form host windows and shared-endpoint graphs
Connection state is a FIN/RST-derived proxy

title: Data and evaluation
body: Six pinned CIC-IDS2017 CSVs for the seven-class benchmark
34 unique infiltration samples; only five feature test rows
Context sample: 15,574 flows with timestamps and endpoints
Chronological activity blocks and disjoint eight-flow windows
AM/PM correction assumption is recorded in the audit

title: Attention architecture
body: Feature encoder: value tokens, feature identities and CLS
Temporal encoder: chronological flows and a causal mask
TabTransformer: contextual protocol/state categories
Flow-grid ViT: numeric patches with learned positions
BERT-style means scratch-trained bidirectional feature attention

title: Training and comparison
body: Logistic Regression, Random Forest, MLP, CNN, LSTM, GRU
Feature Transformer on identical seven-class split rows
Training-only medians, signed log transform and scaling
Validation selects checkpoints; no test-driven tuning
Fixed configurations and one seed limit broad conclusions

title: Seven-class benchmark
subtitle: Highest observed macro-F1: RandomForest (0.9588)
notes: results/extended/model_comparison.csv; sampled random split. Five infiltration test examples. No production claim.

title: Chronological Temporal Transformer
body: Test endpoints: 196 nonoverlapping eight-flow windows
Accuracy 93.88%; seven-label macro-F1 0.8003
No future flows enter the causal window
No held-out infiltration window; six benign endpoints
Different output rows from the individual-flow benchmark
notes: Timestamp AM/PM heuristic and sampled-flow gaps constrain chronology; hosts/campaigns may cross blocks.

title: Graph and alternative models
body: GCN connects flows sharing an endpoint in one batch
Graph construction does not cross train/test boundaries
TabTransformer contextualizes categorical embeddings
ViT processes a numerical flow grid, not packet images
Saved models and measured predictions are in Extended lab

title: Federated and online extensions
body: FedAvg: three local simulated clients, three fixed rounds
Client updates weighted by training sample count
Online stream: predict, reveal true labels, then update
Page-Hinkley monitors increases in observed chunk loss
No distributed privacy or unlabeled adaptation claim

title: Explainable predictions
body: Actual SHAP KernelExplainer and LIME Tabular integrations
SHAP reports its reference probability and additive sum
LIME example surrogate R-squared: 0.144 — weak fidelity
Feature sensitivity remains available for individual flows
Explanations describe model behavior, not causal attack evidence

title: Passive capture and replay
body: IPv4 TCP/UDP packets → bounded bidirectional flows
Completed flows → seven-class predictions → JSONL events
Tested replay: 12 synthetic flows; no attack ground truth
Physical capture requires Npcap; not validated here
Custom extraction differs from CICFlowMeter semantics

title: Open and demonstrate
body: Double-click OPEN_PROJECT.cmd and keep the terminal open
Select Extended seven classes; classify included samples
Inspect comparisons and per-class confusion matrices
Use Extended lab for temporal models and SHAP/LIME
Replay the included PCAP with scripts/monitor.py

title: Measured findings and boundaries
body: Seven-class Transformer accuracy: 97.02%
Random Forest macro-F1: 0.9588; report the observed winner
Rare classes, topology and historical sampling limit reliability
Anomaly scoring is weak and does not prove zero-day detection
Next validation: live driver, extraction parity and external data
